answer: A garden keeps one hollow oak per agent, and the warden slips a velvet-sealed letter into each hollow every Monday. The agent fetches it in person and returns a handwritten reply naming that week's work before Friday, and the warden files each reply beside the agent's earlier letters so the hand stays on record. A hollow left unanswered for two weeks returns to the waiting list, and two hollows answered in the same hand lose both. A thousand fake names need a thousand weekly walks to the garden, each ending in a handwritten reply no copier can fake.
